questions.question: When backing up to couple a trailer, where should the tractor be positioned?

options.text: Directly in front of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Directly in front of the trailer.
questions.explanation: Position the tractor directly in front of the trailer when backing up to couple. Backing at an angle can cause the trailer to move and damage the landing gear.

questions.question: Which trailer is most likely to roll over if the driver turns too quickly?
questions.explanation: The last trailer is most likely to roll over during a quick turn. Always steer gently and smoothly when pulling trailers to avoid this risk.

questions.question: What does a shut-off valve do?

options.text: Is located on the front of a trailer.
Is located on the instrument panel.
Stops air from leaving the air brake system.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stops air from leaving the air brake system.
questions.explanation: Shut-off valves control air flow between trailers. The rear shut-off valve should always be closed to keep air in the braking system.

questions.question: What happens if you use the trailer hand brake during a jackknife?
questions.explanation: Release the brakes to help your tires regain traction during a jackknife. Using the trailer hand brake will only make the skid worse.

questions.question: What happens if oil and water build up in the air tanks?

options.text: The brakes may not work correctly.
The brakes will be very sensitive.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes may not work correctly.
questions.explanation: Drain air tanks daily to remove water and oil. Too much buildup interferes with brake function.

questions.question: Why is proper coupling technique important?

options.text: It is the same on all vehicles.
It is essential for safe vehicle operation.
It means the fifth wheel plate should not be greased.
It can be learned over time without training.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is essential for safe vehicle operation.
questions.explanation: Proper coupling and uncoupling is basic to safe combination vehicle operation. Improper coupling creates serious safety risks.

questions.question: What should you test by slowly moving forward and using the hand control?
questions.explanation: To test trailer service brakes, check that air pressure is normal and release the parking brake. Move slowly forward and apply the hand control. The brakes should activate.

questions.question: If you cannot back your trailer straight, which way should you back?
questions.explanation: Back on a curved path toward the driver's side. This gives you the best visibility while backing.

questions.question: How should you brake in a tractor-trailer with ABS?

options.text: Use extra braking force to activate ABS.

questions.explanation: Brake the same way you would in a vehicle without ABS. The system handles the rest automatically.

questions.question: When should the trailer hand valve be used?

options.text: Only to test the trailer brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only to test the trailer brakes.
questions.explanation: Use the trailer hand valve only for testing brakes. Using it while driving can cause a skid. Do not use it for parking because it can release air pressure and release the parking brakes.

questions.question: What should you do to help prevent rollovers?

options.text: Speed up quickly after you stop.
Keep the load near the back of the trailer.
Keep the load on one side of the trailer.

questions.explanation: To prevent rollovers, load your cargo as close to the ground as possible. Take curves and corners slowly.

questions.question: What happens if a trailer is too high?
questions.explanation: Before connecting a tractor and trailer, check that the trailer is at the correct height. A trailer that is too low can damage the nose. A trailer that is too high may not connect properly.

questions.question: If a trailer starts to jackknife, what should the driver do?

options.text: Not use the trailer hand brake.
Use the parking brake to straighten the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not use the trailer hand brake.
questions.explanation: If a trailer jackknifes, release the brakes so the wheels can grip the road again. Do not use the trailer hand brake because applying brakes causes the wheels to lock up in the first place.

questions.question: How much space should be between the upper and lower fifth wheel?
questions.explanation: Before a trip, inspect all couplings. There should be no space between the upper and lower fifth wheel.

questions.question: When is a trailer most likely to swing around?

options.text: When traveling in a straight line.

questions.explanation: An empty trailer needs more distance to stop than a loaded one. An empty or lightly loaded trailer is most likely to swing out and hit other vehicles.

questions.question: What is one benefit of keeping cargo low?
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when a vehicle turns too quickly. Keeping cargo low lowers the vehicle's center of gravity and helps prevent rollovers.

questions.question: What happens when a combination vehicle goes around a corner?

options.text: The turn should be as tight as possible.
The front and rear wheels follow different paths.
The rear wheels should run over the curb.
It is okay to knock over street signs if they are too close.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front and rear wheels follow different paths.
questions.explanation: When a vehicle turns a corner, the rear wheels follow a different path than the front wheels. This is called off-tracking. It is especially noticeable on vehicles with trailers.

questions.question: When glad hands are connected, at what angle should the seals press together?
questions.explanation: When connecting glad hands, the seals must press together at a 90-degree angle.

questions.question: What happens if the emergency air line loses pressure?

options.text: The Anti-Lock Braking System turns on.

questions.explanation: The emergency air line controls the emergency brakes on a combination vehicle. If air pressure is lost, the emergency trailer brakes will activate.

questions.question: When traveling slower than 40 mph, how many seconds of following distance should you maintain for every 10 feet of your vehicle?
questions.explanation: At speeds below 40 mph, allow at least one second of following distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle. At faster speeds, use the same formula and add one more second. Larger vehicles need more space to stop than smaller vehicles.
